title: Beyond sovereignty: nationally led crisis response in East Africa
authors: John Bryant
abstract: In the past two years, the humanitarian sector has contracted by almost one-third because of large falls in funding from public and private donors. While debates as to the how and why of humanitarian reform are not new, the scale of these cuts makes a changed sector now inevitable, though its shape and role continues to be contested.

title: Poverty and public finance: a primer
authors: Martin Evans
abstract: A primer on how poverty is defined, measured and reported and how fiscal policy shapes poverty outcomes.

title: What makes finance ministry officials tick
authors: Gundula Löffler; Andrea Sissa Velandia; Antoine Lacroix
abstract: A survey of 142 finance ministry officials across low- and middle-income countries reveals how they navigate competing budget demands, and who they believe really holds influence over spending decisions.

title: Equitable AI governance for the Global South: a supply chains and value chains approach
authors: Dr Divij Joshi
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly becoming a foundational technology shaping economic growth, labour markets, public services, and knowledge production worldwide. As AI systems are increasingly embedded across sectors – from healthcare and education, to agriculture, finance, and governance – the question of how AI is governed has become a critical global policy concern. While international attention to AI governance has expanded significantly in recent years, existing approaches remain insufficient to address the ways in which AI may widen global inequalities, particularly between high-income countries and the Global South.

title: Does EU aid promote EU exports?
authors: Derrick Abudu; Maximiliano Mendez-Parra; Dirk Willem te Velde
abstract: The next EU budget offers an opportunity to play a leading role in the fight against global poverty. Most rich countries have cut development assistance, global health included, and more cuts seem likely. The EU’s next long-term budget, the Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF) for 2028 to 2034, is one of the few places where development cooperation could hold its own, and one of the few that could fill part of the gap the cuts have left. Whether it does so depends on a negotiation that is far from settled.

title: How LGBTQI+ movements shape inclusive civic space in Pakistan
authors: Ayesha Khan; Sarah Zaman; Ghausia Rashid Salam; Evie Browne
abstract: This report by ODI Global, ALIGN and the Global Philanthropy Project, demonstrates how LGBTQI+ movements have changed civic space in Pakistan, even as their participation is constrained by discriminatory social norms and narrowed opportunities to exercise political voice.

title: Resourcing LGBTQI+ movements in the Global South and East to build inclusive civic space
authors: Evie Browne; Carmen Leon-Himmelstine; Ayesha Khan
abstract: Drawing on research from Pakistan, Thailand and Argentina, this Briefing Paper by ODI Global, ALIGN and the Global Philanthropy Project, argues that investment in LGBTQI+ movements is an investment in a more inclusive civic space – and, ultimately, in democracy.

title: The Taliban’s madrassa system in Afghanistan: the threat to global peace and security
authors: Ayesha Khan; Mariam Safi
abstract: The Taliban’s development of an ideologically driven madrassa education system could pose risks to global peace and security. This ODI Policy Brief warns global policymakers about the implications of this emerging system.

title: Public finance in the digital era: emerging themes 2026
authors: Ameya Ashok Naik
abstract: Governments are navigating rapid technological change alongside tighter fiscal constraints, declining aid and growing pressure to mobilise domestic resources. At the same time, investments in digital systems have not always delivered the expected improvements in public financial management.

title: Defining progress in domestic capital market development
authors: Grant Metcalfe-Smith; Andrea Carvajal
abstract: Domestic capital markets are increasingly central to how African economies finance development, but what does "progress" actually look like, and who gets to define it?

title: Community resilience and inclusion in protracted crises: lessons from the Syrian civil war
authors: Ian D. Quick
abstract: This case study discusses support to community resilience and economic inclusion during the Syria crisis for the period 2020–2024.

title: Programme of work - IDA Technical Working Group
abstract: The International Development Association (IDA) sits at the heart of concessional finance for the world's lowest-income countries. Yet shifting development needs, mounting debt vulnerabilities, increasing climate and economic shocks and a rapidly evolving global financing landscape are raising fundamental questions about how IDA can remain fit for purpose.

title: Climate change is driving up loss and damage in SIDS
authors: Emily Wilkinson; Vikrant Panwar
abstract: Small Island Developing States (SIDS) experience higher levels of loss and damage from extreme weather in relation to their gross domestic product (GDP) than any other group of countries. And new data suggests that an increasingly high proportion of these losses can be directly attributed to climate change.

title: Raising FDI for African manufacturing: an assessment of Manufacturing Africa’s additionality
authors: Linda Calabrese; Tiina Pasanen; Derrick Abudu; Courtney Lindsay; Anushka Sisodia; Dirk Willem te Velde
abstract: How can public funds catalyse large‑scale private investment in African manufacturing?

title: Refugee camps: current practice and historical perspectives
authors: Benjamin Thomas White; Kerrie Holloway
abstract: This outcome note details the reflection, discussion and learning that were generated in a series of workshops, funded by the Council for British Research in the Levant, that sought to bring together stakeholders from a wide range of organisations led by and supporting refugees.

title: Financing the frontline: how health facilities receive, manage and utilise financial resources in six low- and middle-income countries
authors: Tom Hart; Danielle Serebro; Antoine Lacroix
abstract: A new cross-country analysis examines how financing reaches primary health care (PHC) facilities in six countries — Burkina Faso, Indonesia, Kenya, Pakistan (Khyber Pakhtunkhwa), the Philippines, and Uganda — and how public financial management (PFM) systems influence facilities' ability to use these resources. The study explores funding sources and flows, the PFM rules governing access and spending, and the types of expenditures that PHC facilities are permitted to make.

title: Making an exception: maintaining ODA eligibility for Small Island Developing States
authors: Vikrant Panwar; Gail Hurley; Emily Wilkinson; Aditi Solanki; Johari Weaver
abstract: This working paper is by the Resilient and Sustainable Islands Initiative ( RESI) , within the Global Risks and Resilience programme.

title: Background analysis of climate risks to Syria’s electricity and urban water sectors
authors: Sarah Opitz-Stapleton; Magda Nassef; Camille Laville; Jim Jarvie; Yue Cao; Basile Maupu-Estupina; Mauricio Vazquez
abstract: This report brings together new analysis of Syria’s climate trends, population scenarios, water systems and electricity demand to inform risk-informed reconstruction planning through 2045 and beyond.

title: Tax expenditure report: Rwanda
authors: Romal Sanjeeda; Harshil Parekh
abstract: The Rwandan Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning (MINECOFIN) has published its FY2024-25 Tax Expenditure Report as part of the FY2026–2029 Executive Budget Proposal. Marking the eighth consecutive year of tax expenditure reporting, it highlights the Government's commitment to fiscal transparency.

title: The political economy of education system (in)coherence in Jordan
authors: Olya Homonchuk; Caterina Mazzilli; Tim Kelsall
abstract: This analysis was completed in February 2025 and should be read as a political economy snapshot of that period. While the context has continued to evolve since, many of the underlying incentives and institutional dynamics remain relevant.

title: Has the World Bank really ‘accelerated’ 50 million electricity connections in Africa?
authors: Bright Simons
abstract: This briefing argues that the World Bank and African Development Bank have overstated Mission 300's impact by attributing 50 million electricity connections to the initiative, when most of these connections stem from projects that were approved and financed long before Mission 300 was launched. A review of project reports across six African countries found no evidence of a post-launch acceleration in electrification, suggesting that the claimed surge reflects the natural completion phase of existing programmes rather than new delivery driven by Mission 300.

title: North Stars for Northern Donors in a Post-Aid World: moving from dialogue to decisions
authors: Nilima Gulrajani
abstract: How should Northern donors evolve over the next decade?

title: Gender norms and protection: navigating agency, risk and backlash
authors: Anki Sjöberg; Ján Michalko; Gemma Davies
abstract: Conflict exacerbates and creates gendered inequalities and risks rooted in gender norms. At the same time, people exercise their agency to strengthen their protection by actively drawing on, adapting or challenging gender norms as part of their self-protection strategies. These strategies are complex and highly context-specific, but share a common feature: they rely on an implicit understanding that gender shapes risk, power and legitimacy.

title: Comparing tax and benefit microsimulation models: a guide for analysts in low- and middle-income countries
authors: Laura Abramovsky; Martin Evans; Abdul Malik Iddrisu; Martin Mikloš; David Philips
abstract: Distributional analysis is a crucial component of policymaking. Distributional models estimate who gains from and who bears the costs of different tax and benefit policies. They can provide a detailed diagnostic assessment of the existing fiscal system, help identify areas for reform, and model the impacts of proposed reforms and alternative policy scenarios. This helps policymakers understand the distributional, poverty, and inequality impacts of different policies and their combinations.

title: Oppression, liberation and humanitarianism in Palestine, Myanmar and Sudan
authors: Nora Hassanien; Manny Maung; Dustin Barter
abstract: This paper examines how historical and contemporary settler colonialism, compounded by predatory capitalism, drive extreme violence and vast humanitarian needs in Palestine, Myanmar and Sudan. They are not accidental crises but manufactured and sustained by oppressive power systems and malicious actors.

title: ODI Europe Impact Report: Bridging Europe and the world in a fragmented era
abstract: Europe's role in the world is being tested, renegotiated, and reshaped in real time. As geopolitical rivalry intensifies, economic security reshapes strategic choices, and multilateral cooperation grows more contested, the assumptions that once underpinned European policymaking no longer hold. Our new impact report sets out how ODI Europe has worked over the past year to help Europe and its partners navigate this more complex and interconnected global landscape.

title: The EU–Malawi partnership: outlook for EU development cooperation
authors: Claire Kumar; Davide Fina
abstract: Following the announcement of the Global Gateway strategy and the EU’s new strategic agenda, Europe’s political priorities have shifted.

title: Delivering an ecosystem approach to humanitarian action: proposals from the Advisory Panel on the Future of Humanitarian Action
abstract: The humanitarian system is facing a crisis of legitimacy. Recent funding trends highlight how the system, built for short-term emergencies, is now expected to manage the consequences of long-term political failure. Not only are humanitarian needs driven by underlying factors that rely on power imbalances and a lack of accountability, but the system is failing to provide answers to these as its own accountability is to the current power-holders and not to affected people.

title: Getting funds to the front-line: Uganda's experience with DFF
authors: Antoine Lacroix; Angellah Nakyanzi; Martin Wabwire; Keren Chebet; Derrick Semukasa; Tom Hart
abstract: Primary health facilities in low- and lower-middle-income countries often struggle to receive operational funding reliably and on time. Direct Facility Financing (DFF) - where funds are channelled directly to facilities to cover part of their running costs - has gained growing attention as a practical alternative to more complex, donor-driven financing models.

title: Delivering on gender equality: the missing piece in climate and food systems policy
authors: Maryam Rezaei; Shahzoda Alikhanova
abstract: Agrifood systems face a convergence of global challenges: an accelerating climate crisis, rapid biodiversity and ecosystem loss, rising fragility and conflict and geopolitical shifts, all of which are reshaping the financial and political commitment underpinning international development cooperation.

title: Online violence against women in politics: what shapes political party responses to technology-facilitated gender-based violence?
authors: Ján Michalko; Diana Jiménez Thomas Rodriguez
abstract: Over the last decade, a new threat to democracy has emerged in the form of technology-facilitated gender-based violence (TFGBV). While women in politics and LGBTQI+ people have long faced barriers to their participation in public life rooted in unequal gender norms, the scale and spread of TFGBV poses a significant threat to democracies worldwide because of its silencing and chilling effects.

title: The State of SIDS Report 2026: defending the special case
authors: Eliorah Malifa; Emily Wilkinson; Jack Corbett; Matthew Bishop; Gail Hurley; Courtney Lindsay; Rachid Bouhia; George Carter
abstract: The inaugural State of SIDS Report from the Resilient and Sustainable Islands Initiative (RESI) at ODI Global. The report offers a comprehensive overview of the challenges and opportunities facing Small Island Developing States (SIDS) at a pivotal moment for climate resilience and sustainable development, making a clear case for the continuation of targeted development assistance.

title: Green trade, regional value chains and new partnerships for cooperation: accelerating green industrialisation through partnerships with a focus on Africa
authors: Jodie Keane; Bernardo Arce Fernandez
abstract: Global trade is being reshaped by a new ‘security–sustainability’ nexus. As supply chains are reconfigured for resilience, regional partnerships are becoming central to economic growth and green transformation.

title: Implementation of the AfCFTA Protocol on Investment: a stocktake of promotion and facilitation provisions and potential effects on textiles and garments value chains
authors: Bernardo Arce Fernandez; Derrick Abudu; Roslyn Ng’eno; Dirk Willem te Velde; Faizel Ismail; Bruce Byiers; Poorva Karkare; Mouhamadou Madana Kane; Dode Seidu; Paul Baker; Smita Bheenick; Fahd Azaroual; Saloi El Yamani
abstract: countries translate continental legal commitments into actual cross-border investments and stronger regional value chains?

title: Undertaking AfCFTA gap analyses: what are we learning?
authors: Dirk Willem te Velde; Bernardo Arce Fernandez; Derrick Abudu; Yohannes Ayele; Maximiliano Mendez-Parra; Roslyn Ng’eno; Fahd Azaroual; Paul Baker; Smita Bheenick; Damon Bristow; Mary Chege; Mag-Teerey Ibrahim; Mouhamadou Madana Kane; Charity Korir; Manfred Kouty; Arnaud N’Goran; Dode Seidu; Abdou Touray; Zizwe Paul Vilane
abstract: The AfCFTA Protocol on Investment, adopted in February 2023, requires State Parties to progressively align their national investment laws and frameworks within five years of its entry into force. This report presents the structured gap analysis methodology developed jointly by the AfCFTA Secretariat and ODI Global to assess how national and regional investment regimes align with the Protocol’s provisions.

title: Gender equality and the climate crisis: resolutions at the Human Rights Council
authors: Amy Cano Prentice; Evie Browne; Brianna Craft; Donya Khosravi
abstract: Since 2008, the Human Rights Council (HRC) has brought a human rights lens to climate action, playing a leading role in analysing and recognising the links between climate change and human rights.

title: The value of debt pause clauses
authors: Tom Hart; Andrea Carvajal
abstract: When disasters hit, sovereign borrowers need breathing room - not more debt. This paper estimates what would have happened if seven middle-income countries had debt pause clauses embedded in their bonds at the time of recent major shocks.

title: Eight considerations for adaptation finance quality discussions
authors: Nella Canales; Lina Adil; Natalia Daza Niño; Iyaloo Akuaake
abstract: The Finance Working Group (FWG) is an open partnership bringing together a range of independent expert perspectives from the global north and south on the progress made toward financing climate action. This paper was written by FWG members.

title: Climate action as peace enabler: lessons from the Sahel on delivering peace and social dividends in fragile settings
authors: Camille Laville; Leigh Mayhew; Maman Noura Idi Mamadou; Amir Khouzam
abstract: This case study examines the Justice and Stability in the Sahel (JASS) programme in Mali and Niger to explore whether climate action in the Sahel can generate broader peace and social benefits alongside enhanced resilience.

title: Diversification of household activities among cotton-farming households in southern Mali
authors: Boukary Barry; Dansiné Diarra; Marta Eichsteller; Kougba Sangaré; Joseph Sanou; Steve Wiggins
abstract: Farming households across Mali have long diversified their activities to make the most of available labour and buffer against risk. But from 2010 onwards, cotton yields have been in decline and incomes have stagnated. As a result, the pressure to diversify and find new sources of income has never been greater for households in southern parts of the country.

title: How cotton farmers escape poverty by diversification in India and Mali. Intersecting crises and supports
authors: Steve Wiggins; Lucia da Corta; Boukary Barry; Dansiné Diarra; Marta Eichsteller; Uppalapati Janatha; Jacob Kalle; P.V. Neelima Rao; Kougba Sangaré; Joseph Sanou; Davuluri Venkateswarlu
abstract: This synthesis report combines findings from two country-based studies on the barriers and enablers to household income diversification for cotton farmers in India and Mali.

title: Pathways out of poverty through cotton farmer diversification in India amid climate, economic and political change
authors: Lucia da Corta; Davuluri Venkateswarlu; Steve Wiggins; Marta Eichsteller; Jacob Kalle; Uppalapati Janatha; P.V. Neelima Rao
abstract: Cotton farming has become increasingly precarious for smallholders in India. Rising input costs, variable weather patterns, pest issues, and volatile prices have squeezed margins. At the same time, growing household cost have deepened economic vulnerability.

title: Ensuring the Global Partnerships Conference delivers for countries affected by conflict and fragility
abstract: Ahead of the Global Partnerships Conference (May 2026), ODI Global and the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) convened a select group of over sixty participants and experts from the private sector, IFIs, foundations, states, NGOs, and academia, to explore the barriers and, crucially, opportunities to strengthen partnership approaches, and to diversify and increase financial flows specifically to FCAS, in ways that contribute effectively to building stability and resilience. Participants were also able to share examples of investment partnerships that had worked and could be scaled as captured by the summary document presented below.

title: ODI Global Strategy, 2026-2031
abstract: At a decisive moment for global cooperation, ODI Global is launching a new five-year strategy focused on advancing equity and justice in a rapidly changing world.

title: The impact of climate change on education outcomes: a systematic review
authors: Akanksha Bapna; Rachel Marcus; Diana Jiménez Thomas Rodriguez; Donya Khosravi
abstract: Human-caused climate change is driving extreme weather events at increasing frequency and scale - including droughts, fires, and temperature and flooding. These events cause significant damage to life, infrastructure, health, nutrition, and education. With the world currently on track for 2.7°C of warming this century, nearly double the 1.5°C global target, it is the most vulnerable people and systems that bear the greatest burden of these impacts.

title: The state of international humanitarian funding to local and national actors
authors: Mike Pearson; Niklas Rieger
abstract: Increasing funding to local and national actors (LNAs) is one of the core humanitarian reform areas of the last decade. The Grand Bargain set out a collective commitment of 25% of humanitarian funding going to LNAs.

title: Airports and aviation emissions
authors: Shandelle Steadman; Sam Pickard
abstract: This policy brief accompanies the 2026 Airport Tracker : a global inventory of CO2 and local air pollutants at the airport level aimed at highlighting the climate impact of the world’s largest airports.

title: Practicalities of humanitarian action in contexts of internal displacement
authors: Caitlin Sturridge; Leen Fouad; Kerrie Holloway
abstract: This chapter of The Oxford Handbook of Internal Displacement examines the complex humanitarian landscape surrounding internally displaced persons (IDPs), focusing on key challenges in addressing their needs and vulnerabilities.

title: Reimagining donorship: The Donors in a Post-Aid World dialogue series
authors: Heba Aly; Nilima Gulrajani; Jessica Pudussery
abstract: Between October 2024 and May 2026, ODI Global convened a series of five dialogues to reimagine and co-create a new vision for Northern donors in the 21st century. Over 18 months, the Donors in a Post-Aid World (dPAW) dialogue series brought together bilateral DAC donors with a rotating group of thinkers, activists and government officials cutting across geographic boundaries of North and South. Together they discussed and debated both what that vision should look like, and how it might be operationalised. The objective was to provide a space for creative, out-of-the-box thinking on the role of Northern donors at a time when many were asking questions about the purpose and effectiveness of aid.

title: Supporting just transitions through social protection: key roles for philanthropy
authors: Anna McCord; Emma Gogerty
abstract: This briefing paper by Global Risks and Resilience looks at how philanthropies can contribute to ensuring a just transition to net zero, through the extension of social protection to address poverty and income security.

title: Climate risks to Syria’s electricity systems
authors: Sarah Opitz-Stapleton; Yue Cao; Camille Laville; Elena Kiryakova; Basile Maupu-Estupina; Jim Jarvie; Mauricio Vazquez
abstract: The restoration and expansion of electricity generation and transmission is critical for post-war Syria’s socioeconomic recovery. Restoring and building out the generating and transmission capacity with the future in mind - accounting for population return, economic aspirations and climate change - will determine the country’s economic growth trajectory in coming decades.

title: Climate risks to Syria’s urban water and sanitation systems
authors: Sarah Opitz-Stapleton; Magda Nassef; Jim Jarvie; Basile Maupu-Estupina; Camille Laville; Yue Cao; Mauricio Vazquez
abstract: Syria was already facing a net national water deficit prior to its 14-year civil war. How the country reconstructs its urban water and sanitation sector and manages urban and agricultural demand will shape its water, food and energy security for decades to come.

title: Local currency donor-backed solutions: an evaluation
authors: Grant Metcalfe-Smith; Bianca Getzel; Andrea Carvajal; Frederique Dahan; Daniele Myallonnier
abstract: Local currency financing is vital for emerging markets, yet donors currently lack a clear framework for assessing these complex solutions. This paper proposes three criteria for success: broad viability, contribution to capital market development and cost-efficient use of funds.

title: Gender equality and the climate crisis: champions and backsliders
authors: Brianna Craft; Donya Khosravi; Evie Browne; Amy Cano Prentice
abstract: Multilateralism is facing unprecedented challenges. The gender–climate nexus sits at the intersection of these pressures.

title: Anti-gender & anti-climate politics: exploring converging agendas in Global Majority countries
authors: Diana Jiménez Thomas Rodriguez; Rachel George; Ayesha Khan
abstract: Politics today is marked by accelerating global backlash against both gender equality and action on the climate crisis. This new working paper exposes how these two agendas are increasingly converging in Global Majority countries.

title: Delivering on adaptation finance goals: six recommendations for closing the gap
authors: Kamleshan Pillay; Emily Wilkinson; Mairi Dupar
abstract: Climate adaptation finance remains far below what is needed. This working paper, produced as part of the Climate Ambition Support Alliance (CASA) , assesses progress against key global adaptation finance and climate finance goals, including the Global Goal on Adaptation and the New Collective Quantified Goal on Climate Finance

title: Extreme and erratic weather: climate adaptation in urban displacement
authors: Kerrie Holloway
abstract: Extreme and erratic weather events, many of which are increasing in frequency and intensity due to climate change, have long been seen as both a current and future driver of displacement – displacement that is more likely to be internal than across borders, and more likely to be towards urban areas.

title: Financing climate-responsive social protection: opportunities for leveraging philanthropic capital
authors: Vikrant Panwar; Andrea Sissa Velandia; Emily Wilkinson
abstract: This briefing paper by Global Risks and Resilience examines how financing for climate-responsive social protection needs to evolve under rising climate and transition pressures, and how philanthropies could enable and catalyse such change.

title: Transforming social protection for irreversible climate change-induced loss and damage: key roles for philanthropy
authors: Shandelle Steadman; Harshita Sinha
abstract: This briefing paper by Global Risks and Resilience examines the role of social protection systems in responding to irreversible climate-induced loss and damage and highlights the key role philanthropy can play in transforming these systems to better support populations that can no longer adapt to the impacts of climate change.

title: Reforming multilateral development banks: perspectives from IDA countries
authors: Fatlum Zeka; Annalisa Prizzon

title: Somali systems: from aid-centred to state-led crisis response
authors: Surer Mohamed; Dustin Barter
abstract: There are major challenges in transitioning towards state-led crisis response in Somalia. These include the outsized role of aid and incentive structures that impede the transition towards state leadership.

title: Cost-effective climate change mitigation in low- and middle-income countries: rapid umbrella review
authors: Prashant Vaze; Elizabeth Tan; Elena Kiryakova; Shandelle Steadman; Steve Wiggins
abstract: This rapid umbrella review analyses evidence from scholarly and grey literature on the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of interventions to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions applicable to low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).

title: Healthy islands and islanders: towards a new paradigm for integrating climate change, food security and nutrition in Small Island Developing States
authors: Maryam Rezaei; Matthew Bishop; Merisa Thompson
abstract: As climate change intensifies, small island nations are facing growing threats to their food security. This policy brief from the Resilient and Sustainable Islands Initiative (RESI) looks at how climate, food, and policy are often treated separately, and why that needs to change. It highlights the unique pressures shaping island food systems and sets out a roadmap for more joined-up thinking, investment, and action.

title: Cross-border digital payments and identity in Nigeria under the AfCFTA
authors: Prachi Agarwal; Maximiliano Mendez-Parra; Sand Mba Kalu; Lola Aworanti- Ekugo; Ayobami Olajide
abstract: As the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) transitions from ambition to implementation, Nigeria stands at the forefront of the continent’s digital transformation.

title: How does climate change affect educational outcomes? Key pathways
authors: Rachel Marcus; Akanksha Bapna; Diana Jiménez Thomas Rodriguez; Donya Khosravi
abstract: Human-induced climate change is driving more frequent and intense extreme weather events, which increasingly threaten children's access to education and their learning outcomes.

title: Reforming multilateral development banks: perspectives from client countries
authors: Annalisa Prizzon; Fatlum Zeka; Hayk Gyuzalyan; Arpine Aghjoyan
abstract: Drawing on nearly 650 government and MDB officials across 125 countries and 250 in-depth interviews in 12 countries.

title: The case for large cash transfers: supporting refugees to meet basic needs and build resilience
authors: Kerrie Holloway
abstract: The humanitarian sector has been asking for more humanitarian cash assistance for decades, and the evidence base for this modality is strong. Yet the call for cash assistance to be given as large, multipurpose cash transfers rather than monthly subsistence payments or fragmented sectoral cash is still relatively new.

title: The impacts of climate change on education outcomes: assessment and response
authors: Diana Jiménez Thomas Rodriguez; Rachel Marcus; Akanksha Bapna; Donya Khosravi
abstract: This brief presents findings from a global systematic review examining how climate change affects primary and secondary education across low-, middle- and high-income countries.

title: Effects of early life exposure to climate shocks on education outcomes
authors: Akanksha Bapna; Rachel Marcus; Donya Khosravi; Diana Jiménez Thomas Rodriguez
abstract: Human-induced climate change is driving more frequent and intense extreme weather events — and the consequences stretch far beyond the environment. With global temperatures on track to reach 2.7°C above pre-industrial levels within the next century, far exceeding the 1.5°C target, climate change represents a profound intergenerational threat to human development.

title: Governing inequality: Kenya's state, aid politics and perpetual humanitarian crisis
authors: Zainab Moallin; Korow Dahir Issak; Dustin Barter
abstract: Is the aid industry helping to perpetuate historical and geographic inequalities in Kenya and posing a barrier to state-led crisis response? Why have other middle-income countries taken leadership of humanitarian responses, yet Kenya remains heavily reliant on international assistance? What can be done to galvanise change amid major aid cuts and calamity?

title: Dialogue #4: How to be a donor in a post-aid world
authors: Heba Aly; Nilima Gulrajani; Jessica Pudussery
abstract: Co-hosted with the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the Hague on 27-28 January 2026, this dPAW fourth dialogue brought together donor officials from bilateral aid and multilateral policy departments, civil society actors, researchers and thinkers to explore how Northern donors must evolve their institutions and operations in a world where their partners seek greater autonomy and sovereignty, where aid is likely a smaller development finance flow, and where eventually donors may not need to exist at all.

title: What can development finance institutions learn from new growth theories?
abstract: As shareholders push development finance institutions (DFIs) to operate in places where private sector growth is scarce, a foundational question has gone largely unanswered: what theory of growth actually underpins how DFIs invest?

title: Better software options for public financial management
authors: James Stewart; Lauren Kahn; Cathal Long

title: How underfunding local organisations' overheads undermines humanitarian action
authors: Nora Hassanien; Mike Pearson
abstract: Local and national humanitarian actors (LNAs) are often the first and last responders during a crisis, yet they continue to operate within a system that systematically underfunds their safety, organisational health and sustainability.

title: China’s economic footprint in Latin America and the Caribbean
authors: Elena Kiryakova; Karen Jackson; Rebecca Nadin
abstract: This research report by the Global Risks and Resilience programme, examines the evolution of China’s trade, lending and outward foreign direct investment in Latin America and the Caribbean since 2013, by combining several data sources for the first time.

title: Community-led negotiations
authors: Katherine Kramer
abstract: It is now recognised that communities are not just victims or passive actors in armed conflict. They have agency and, in many cases, through direct dialogue they have influenced authorities and armed actors in favour of restraint, or to allow access to the resources and services communities need for their survival. In fact, local communities may exercise considerable influence over armed actors at the local level.

title: Protection negotiations with armed actors
authors: Pascal Bongard
abstract: Negotiations with armed actors have long been a component in the humanitarian toolkit, often part of a broader dialogue or engagement strategy. However, negotiations to strengthen the protection of civilians are not uniformly undertaken or consistently carried out in humanitarian action, despite long-standing commitments to humanitarian diplomacy to strengthen protection.

title: Additional resources - ERICC conference 2026
abstract: In the lead up to ODI Global and ERICC's conference, Reimagining financing in conflict-affected settings: lessons from education , health and social protection, we have put together a list of additional resources to frame the conversations around the event.

title: Education and economic opportunities for refugee and displaced youth in Chad
authors: Veronique Barbelet; Kerrie Holloway; Carmen Leon-Himmelstine; Colette Benoudji
abstract: This report examines the landscape of the secondary school education system, transitional pathways to dignified and fulfilling work, and the policy changes necessary for the self-reliance of forcibly displaced young people in Chad.

title: Advancing gender rights at the Human Rights Council in times of backlash
authors: Ayesha Khan; Ján Michalko
abstract: In a context of high polarisation and long-term tensions over advancing gender equality, this report examines how negotiations at the 59th session of the Human Rights Council in June 2025 achieved some key successes, and managed to hold the line on gender rights in the face of backlash.

title: MDBs as an asset class
authors: Chris Humphrey; Chris McHugh
abstract: Multilateral development banks (MDBs) are under growing pressure to mobilise far greater volumes of private capital for emerging and developing economies. In response, they are experimenting with new instruments, partners and balance sheet techniques - prompting some observers to ask whether MDBs are becoming an asset class in their own right.

title: Preferred creditor treatment and multilateral development banks’ mobilisation agenda
authors: Chris Humphrey; Jessica Pudussery; Frederique Dahan
abstract: Preferred creditor treatment (PCT) is a cornerstone of the multilateral development bank (MDB) model. It reflects the long-standing expectation that sovereign borrowers prioritise repaying MDB loans - even in times of financial distress - and that other creditors accept the exclusion of MDB loans from sovereign debt restructurings. PCT underpins MDBs’ financial strength, supports their high credit ratings and allows them to borrow at favourable terms in global capital markets.

title: How to manage crises differently in ASALs without talking about a nexus: what we can learn from the water sector
authors: Simon Levine
abstract: Produced as part of Supporting Pastoralism and Agriculture in Recurrent and Protracted Crises (SPARC), research on water development in the drylands reveals how a divide between development thinking and humanitarian action is undermining resilience and community trust.

title: Transition finance across G20 presidencies
authors: Archie Gilmour; Shandelle Steadman; Amy Cano Prentice; Mirza Sadaqat Huda
abstract: Transitioning to an economy powered by renewable energy is a significant challenge. It requires enormous technological and political will - as well as investment targeting the right areas, or 'transition finance'. But the world is undergoing a seismic shift, with old alliances fracturing and the multilateral system creaking. As a result, the transition to a sustainable economy is slipping down the list of global priorities.

title: A novel protocol for Digital Mineral Information Rights in Africa
authors: Bright Simons
abstract: Africa’s mineral future will not be defined solely by what lies beneath the surface, but by how effectively the continent governs, shares and monetises the information required to discover and evaluate those resources. In the accelerating global competition for critical minerals, the most strategic asset is no longer machinery or concession acreage, but geological intelligence.

title: Europe and Africa flipped the script on industrial minerals
authors: Bright Simons
abstract: One frequently hears that the African continent possesses 30% of the world’s mineral reserves. The figure is wielded as a geopolitical trophy by some and as a stick to beat African leaders by others. The simple geoeconomic fact, however, is that this statistic has no basis in reality.

title: Getting Smart about Africa’s mineral wealth: how Digital Public Infrastructure can revolutionise mineral fiscal regimes in West Africa

title: Negotiating the United Nations Framework Convention on International Tax Cooperation
authors: Courtney Lindsay
abstract: One year on from the start of negotiations on the new UN Tax Convention, Small Island Developing States (SIDS) face a rare and significant opportunity to reform global tax rules - in ways that will benefit small island economies and communities long into the future.

title: Pathways to better funding for women-led organisations
authors: Nicholas Veerapen; Caterina Mazzilli; Megan Daigle
abstract: Women-led organisations (WLOs) are indispensable humanitarian actors whose proximity, trust and gendered analysis enable them to reach people and fulfil priorities that other actors simply cannot. While they share many strengths with other local and national actors, they also have particular strengths rooted in their leadership as women, girls and gender-diverse people who face marginalisation around the world.

title: Addressing spiralling climate and environmental risks in Yemen's Taizz and Hadhramaut governates
authors: Ian D. Quick; Yue Cao; Camille Laville; Basile Maupu-Estupina
abstract: This report shares evidence on climate-related hazards that could worsen conflict and security risks in Yemen, to inform stabilisation, peacebuilding and security interventions.

title: China’s infrastructure finance in Africa: impacts and lessons
authors: Vivien Foster; Roumeen Islam; Yunnan Chen; Linda Calabrese
abstract: China has been a major financier of African infrastructure over the past two decades, supporting large-scale projects in sectors such as hydropower, mining and rail. But this role is changing.

abstract: Which development partners do Small Island Developing States (SIDS) value most, and why?

authors: Mairi Dupar; Courtney Lindsay
abstract: This report, produced as part of a project led by the CLEAN Helpdesk , aims to provide guidance for sustainable blue economy programming in the Caribbean Small Island Developing States region.

authors: Mairi Dupar; Courtney Lindsay
abstract: This report, produced as part of a project led by the CLEAN Helpdesk , aims to provide guidance for sustainable blue economy programming in Pacific small island developing states region, including Timor-Leste.

title: Health budget execution and procurement systems: The state of play in Malawi
authors: Dominic Nkhoma; Alessandro Ramella Pezza; Gerald Manthalu; Bob Muchabaiwa; Tapiwa Kelvin Mutambirwa; Chawezie Kondowe; Precious Chitsulo; Tom Hart
abstract: Malawi’s commitment to achieving Universal Health Coverage (UHC) by 2030 is constrained by weak and unpredictable health financing. With around 70% of public spending flowing through procurement, budget reliability is critical to delivering health services.

title: Improving financial access for non-profit organisations: what we have learned, and the road ahead
authors: Helen Alderson; Leen Fouad
abstract: Since March 2024, ODI Global’s Humanitarian Policy Group (HPG) has convened a series of international, cross-sector dialogues bringing together governments, financial institutions (FIs), and non profit organisations (NPOs) to address financial access challenges faced by NPOs.

title: Food prices in Mali and Sudan: changes, causes, consequences and responses - May 2025 update
authors: Steve Wiggins
abstract: This report, produced as part of Supporting Pastoralism and Agriculture in Recurrent and Protracted Crises (SPARC), builds on earlier SPARC-IDRC research on food prices in Mali and Sudan by looking at subsequent price changes and their drivers, effects, and public responses from 2023 to mid-2025.

title: Access to land and resilience for female Sudanese refugees in Chad: systemic issues and local perceptions
authors: Camille Laville
abstract: This study, produced as part of Supporting Pastoralism and Agriculture in Recurrent and Protracted Crises (SPARC), explores the obstacles to, and opportunities for, Sudanese refugee women in eastern Chad to access land. It examines systemic barriers and how to improve coordination between stakeholders.

title: Safeguarding humanitarian action beyond financial sanctions: the impact of trade sanctions and export controls
authors: Emanuela-Chiara Gillard; Helen Alderson
abstract: Humanitarian organisations often operate in contexts where sanctions have been imposed. While contemporary sanctions aim to be ‘targeted’ only for the persons and entities whose behaviour they aim to change, they continue to adversely impact humanitarian operations.
